questionText:
Consider the database transactions T1 and T2, and data items X and Y. Which of the schedule(s) is/are conflict serializable?

Transaction T1 Transaction T2
R1(X)
W1(Y) W2(X)
R1(X) W2(Y)
W1(X) COMMIT(T2)
COMMIT(T1)
options: R1(X), W2(X), W1(Y), W2(Y), R1(X), W1(X), COMMIT(T2), COMMIT(T1)
W2(X), R1(X), W2(Y), W1(Y), R1(X), COMMIT(T2), W1(X), COMMIT(T1)
R1(X), W1(Y), W2(X), W2(Y), R1(X), W1(X), COMMIT(T1), COMMIT(T2)
W2(X), R1(X), W1(Y), W2(Y), R1(X), COMMIT(T2), W1(X), COMMIT(T1)
explanation:
Step 1: Identify Conflicting Operations
Two operations conflict if they belong to different transactions, operate on the same data item, and at least one of them is a write operation.

Step 2: Construct Precedence Graph for each Schedule

• Schedule (A): R1(X), W2(X), W1(Y), W2(Y), R1(X), W1(X), COMMIT(T2), COMMIT(T1)
- Conflicts on X: R1(X) before W2(X) gives edge $T1 \rightarrow T2$. W2(X) before R1(X) gives edge $T2 \rightarrow T1$.
- Since there is a cycle ($T1 \rightleftharpoons T2$), Schedule (A) is not conflict serializable.

• Schedule (B): W2(X), R1(X), W2(Y), W1(Y), R1(X), COMMIT(T2), W1(X), COMMIT(T1)
- Conflicts on X: W2(X) before R1(X) gives edge $T2 \rightarrow T1$; W2(X) before W1(X) gives edge $T2 \rightarrow T1$.
- Conflicts on Y: W2(Y) before W1(Y) gives edge $T2 \rightarrow T1$.
- There are no edges from $T1 \rightarrow T2$. The precedence graph is acyclic ($T2 \rightarrow T1$). Thus, Schedule (B) is conflict serializable.

• Schedule (C): R1(X), W1(Y), W2(X), W2(Y), R1(X), W1(X), COMMIT(T1), COMMIT(T2)
- Conflicts on X: R1(X) before W2(X) gives edge $T1 \rightarrow T2$. W2(X) before R1(X) gives edge $T2 \rightarrow T1$.
- Contains a cycle ($T1 \rightleftharpoons T2$), so Schedule (C) is not conflict serializable.

• Schedule (D): W2(X), R1(X), W1(Y), W2(Y), R1(X), COMMIT(T2), W1(X), COMMIT(T1)
- Conflicts on X: W2(X) before R1(X) gives edge $T2 \rightarrow T1$.
- Conflicts on Y: W1(Y) before W2(Y) gives edge $T1 \rightarrow T2$.
- Contains a cycle ($T1 \rightleftharpoons T2$), so Schedule (D) is not conflict serializable.

Conclusion:
Only Option (B) is conflict serializable.
